TITLE: Towbar and Trailer Ratings: Evidence to Request Before Buying
PRIMARY_QUERY: towbar towing capacity evidence imported vehicle
SEARCH_INTENT: Decide whether the offered vehicle and fitted towing hardware can support a buyer-defined trailer task.
BUYER_TASK: Compare exact-vehicle capacity evidence, hardware identity, loaded-mass plan and installed electrical functionality before accepting a towing claim.
TARGET_BUYER: Overseas buyers of cars, SUVs and light pickups intended to tow a trailer
WHY_THIS_TOPIC: Distinct installed-system acceptance task rather than broad pickup selection or general VIN inspection.
EXPECTED_DECISION: Accept only documented configuration; request missing proof or reject towing premium.
REFERENCE_MARKET: UK and NSW guidance examples; US Ford and UK Volvo OEM evidence only
FACT_BOUNDARY: No numerical towing rating assigned to any offered vehicle. No global legal requirement or import approval conclusion.

FACTS.claim: Handbook/specification towing limit; train weight includes loaded car and trailer; missing train weight is a stop signal under this guidance.
Vehicle plate distinguishes vehicle, combined and axle limits; coupling, cable and lighting checks.
Towbar approval label identifies approval number and vehicle applicability; first-use-before-1-August-1998 exception.
VIN-based towing calculator and vehicle guides; distinction between vehicle, combination, axle and tongue ratings.
FACTS.scope: US Ford information; not a rating for an export vehicle

FACTS.claim: Towbar can have a higher rating than vehicle; national restrictions can be lower; retrofit may need software update; trailer lighting test described.
Towbar/coupling suitable type and capacity, electrical sockets, brake connections for power/electric brakes; manufacturer/part-number and capacity marking guidance.
FACTS.scope: New South Wales roads; relevant light vehicle procurement examples only
